subject: chemistry
title: Tests for gases
key_idea: Each common gas has its own test. Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop. Oxygen relights a glowing splint. Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky. Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper.

blocks.text: This section covers the two splint tests. They use different splints, so do not mix them up.

items.meaning: A wooden splint with a flame on it.
A wooden splint that has been lit and blown out, so the end glows red.

items: **Hydrogen**: hold a burning splint at the open end of a test tube of the gas.
Hydrogen burns rapidly with a squeaky **pop** sound.
**Oxygen**: put a glowing splint into a test tube of the gas.

sections.heading: Tests for carbon dioxide and chlorine

blocks.text: This section covers the two tests that use a solution or paper.

items.meaning: An aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide.

items: **Carbon dioxide**: shake the gas with limewater, or bubble it through limewater.
**Chlorine**: put damp litmus paper into the gas.
The litmus paper is **bleached** and turns white.
Chlorine: damp litmus paper is bleached white.

checks.q: Describe the test for hydrogen and give the result.
checks.a: Hold a burning (lit) splint at the open end of a test tube of the gas. The gas burns with a (squeaky) pop.

checks.q: A gas turns limewater milky. Name the gas.
checks.a: Carbon dioxide. (Limewater turns milky or cloudy.)

checks.q: Describe the test for chlorine and give the result.
checks.a: Put damp litmus paper into the gas. The litmus paper is bleached (turns white).

worked_example.question:
Ammonia is produced when a mixture of nitrogen and hydrogen reacts.

The mixture of nitrogen and hydrogen must not contain carbon dioxide and oxygen.

Explain how a sample can be tested to show that carbon dioxide is not present in the mixture.
answer_points: The limewater does not turn milky or cloudy (it stays colourless).
worked_example.tip: For a gas that is absent, the result is that nothing changes: limewater stays clear.

worked_example.question:
A student has three solids, A, B and C. The solids are sodium carbonate, powdered zinc and copper oxide, but the student does not know which solid is which.

The student reacted each solid with dilute sulfuric acid. The table shows the student's observations and the results of tests on any gases produced.

Solid | Reaction with dilute sulfuric acid | Gas bubbled through limewater | Gas tested with a lit splint
A | bubbles seen; colourless solution formed | no change | squeaky pop
B | blue solution formed; some black solid remains at bottom of test tube | no gas produced | no gas produced
C | bubbles seen; colourless solution formed | limewater turned cloudy | puts out lit splint

Use the observations and results in the table to identify which solid is which.

Your answer should include
• how each test result helps you to identify the solid
• word equations to support your answer.
answer_points: Solid A is powdered zinc: bubbles show a gas, limewater does not change so it is not carbon dioxide, and the squeaky pop shows hydrogen.
zinc + sulfuric acid → zinc sulfate + hydrogen (metal + acid → salt + hydrogen).
Solid B is copper oxide: no gas is produced, the solid is black, and it forms blue copper sulfate solution.
copper oxide + sulfuric acid → copper sulfate + water.
Solid C is sodium carbonate: bubbles show a gas, and limewater turned cloudy so the gas is carbon dioxide.
sodium carbonate + sulfuric acid → sodium sulfate + carbon dioxide + water.
worked_example.tip: A levelled answer: identify all three solids and link each to its test result for the top level.

blocks.text: Ammonia is a pungent gas. It is alkaline, so it changes the colour of damp litmus paper.

items: Put damp red litmus paper into the gas.
A compound containing ammonium ions gives off ammonia when sodium hydroxide solution is added and the mixture is heated.
Name the gas as ammonia, not ammonium.

blocks.text: With damp blue litmus paper, chlorine first turns the paper red and then bleaches it white.
